facts.text: Ismay was renamed for Isabella and May Earling, daughters of Milwaukee Road president Albert J., after starting as Burt in 1907.
Founded in 1908 amid the expansion of the Chicago, Milwaukee, and Puget Sound Railroad, Ismay became a hub for ranching, farming, and railroad commerce along the Yellowstone Trail.
By the 1980s, the Milwaukee Road abandoned tracks west of Miles City, cutting freight traffic and deepening Ismay’s economic decline.
Proceeds from the Joe Montana stunt funded a fire hall, a fire truck, and the restoration of the historic jail, now part of the Joe Montana Community Center.
